Nataka, all is well in Thousand Needles. The centaur annoyance is nothing more than that...occasionally attacking, nothing substantial as a real threat. However, there does seem to be some news of centaur clans uniting.

We always pondered the threat of a united ruthless race such as the centaur... I try not to dwell on such ideas, as you know... nothing could penetrate the pure hatred they have... even of each other.

-Cliffwatcher Longhorn

Set far back in the Valley of Spears is the holy temple of Maraudon. If that were not transgression enough, you will quickly see why I have asked a non-centaur to aid me in my plight.

There, just beyond the doors where only spirits and our most sacred priests and priestesses may travel is one called The Nameless Prophet. He is the highest of any tribe in spiritual matters and is one of the oldest of any tribe.

The terror of these past few weeks is almost more than I can bear; yet, I feel that by writing down that which I've seen I will somehow be comforted.  So I do it, and it is the only comfort I have these bleak days.

During one such misstep, Erlgadin laid a heavy hand on Barnil's shoulder.  Ajeck and I gave a casual glance, assuming the man was simply giving Barnil a much-needed scolding for his carelessness.  Erlgadin, however, gestured slowly with his head toward a nearby fallen tree.  Gazing back at us were two piercing black eyes just above a mouthful of razor sharp fangs.

On a rocky precipice above, silhouetted by the setting sun, I could make out the largest cat of prey I have ever laid eyes upon.  I was able to loose one clumsy volley with my rifle, but the cat held his ground.  He growled once again, this time louder than the first, and vanished.

We gathered our belongings and headed solemnly back to camp.

We set out at first light, heading south past the Tkashi Ruins.  Barnil voiced concern that we might encounter members of the Bloodscalp Tribe.  I reminded Barnil that the Bloodscalps were more concerned with destroying their tribal enemy, the Skullsplitters.  Needless to say, Barnil was not comforted in the least.  I, however, had a loaded rifle, a satchel full of gunpowder and three deadly hunters with me to ease any concerns of an unfriendly ambush.

Our hastily aimed shots were enough to buy Barnil's escape.  Barnil clamored back down the hill and rejoined the party. We scurried off into the jungle; a pack of ferocious Lashtail Raptor's stalking our every move.

The hunters were now the hunted.

<Impressively, there is a barely legible carving in the remaining skin of the apple.>

Apple yum yum. Me pick flowers now.

To face Frostmaw, you must entice him with the meat of his favorite prey.

Go to the Alterac Mountains in Azeroth and hunt a hulking mountain lion.  Kill it, and then take its carcass to the Growless Cave, a place held sacred by the bestial wendigo.

Place the carcass on the Flame of Uzel and the scent from burning meat will drift from the cave.

And then, in time, Frostmaw will come.

This is the purpose of my book: to catalogue those beings, those otherworldly fiends who would destroy our lands, so that explorers who happen upon them will know what they face.

So if you consider yourself a guardian of Azeroth, then read on.  And know your enemy.

-Ur
Mage of Dalaran

The fiend of which I write is the worgen.

Old, rural folklore may hearken to these creatures, for what farmer's child has not heard tales of beastly wolf-men stalking the woods and marshes outside his village?

And truth may hide in such tales--perhaps they are warnings against the worgen, veiled as myths to frighten us.

But before such tales are dismissed, let me now assure the reader: worgen are real.  They may not be from our world, but avenues exist between their home and ours and powerful magics can pull them here.

Such chants are best left unuttered, for wherever Worgen tread, they bring terror and bloodshed with them.

You will know a worgen by its resemblance to the wolves of our world.  When viewing a worgen one can easily see how its coarse hair, pointed ears and long snout are akin to the wolves we know.

But you will just as quickly see its differences:  that coarse hair surrounds a powerful, two-legged body sporting long fangs and dagger-like claws.  And behind its howl lurks a malevolence possessed by no natural beast.

The worgens' home is a dark place, a place of nightmare.  If that world fosters locales safe from the cursed worgen, then my research has revealed no such bastions.

And if one considers the ferocity and wickedness of the worgen, then it is likely no such bastions exist.

It is surmised that the worgen are content to remain on their world, for although some worgen possess powerful magic, they have made no attempts to reach Azeroth on their own accord.

And for this, we are fortunate.

As mentioned above, some worgen are skilled in mystic arts, and their magic is of darkness and corruption.

Curses and supernatural poisons are common, so be forewarned--those who face worgen magicians should arm themselves with wards against shadow.

It is my hope that no Dalaran wizard seeks out the Worgen, even if done in light conscience.  For no pact may be struck, no secrets may be learned, no good can come from these beasts.

They are best left to their world.  For if found in ours and not destroyed, then our peril will be dire...

$N, below are the items needed to create your armor:

Smokey iron ingots from the Windshear kobolds in the Windshear mine in the Stonetalon Mountains.

Powdered azurite from the Hillsbrad miners in Hillsbrad.

Iron bars from miners, or from iron deposits if you are a miner.

To the Honorable Headmaster Crillian,

My former Master, I write to you so that you might know what your apprentice has been doing of late.  Paying heed to your advice, I sought to build my knowledge and wisdom through travel outside the gates of our beloved Stormwind.  My journeys took me to many places but I have decided to take up residence here in the lovely town of Moonbrook.  The surrounding fields of Westfall are most beautiful as the harvest approaches.

. . .Giles, the boy, seems a bit rambunctious and will be a challenge to educate.  However the elder daughter, Tilloa, seems exceptionally smart.  I couldn't help but to notice her captivating beauty as well.  She is on the cusp of womanhood now.  Supposedly the Lord has arranged her marriage for next year.  But I digress.  This week I will accompany the family to their summer cottage near the Eastvale Logging Camp in Elwynn, close to the Red Ridge Mountains.  I hope to write more while there.

I have found a method to enter the Chamber of Khaz'mul!

Take the Medallion of Gni'kiv from my chest.

Defeat the trogg Revelosh in the chamber before the map room and retrieve the Shaft of Tsol.

Join the medallion and the shaft into the Staff of Prehistoria.

Use the staff in the map room to unlock the door to the Chamber of Khaz'mul.

Do these things, and the chamber will be yours!
-Baelog

As Kil'jaeden prepared the Horde for its invasion of Azeroth, Medivh continued to fight for his soul against Sargeras. King Llane, the noble monarch of Stormwind, grew wary of the darkness which seemed to taint the spirit of his former friend.

1.title: The Dark Portal and the Fall of Stormwind

texts.text: King Llane shared his concerns with Anduin Lothar, the last descendent of the Arathi bloodline, whom he named his lieutenant-at-arms. Even so, neither man could have imagined that Medivh's slow descent into madness would bring about the horrors that were to come.

2.title: The Dark Portal and the Fall of Stormwind

texts.text: As a final incentive, Sargeras promised to bestow great power upon Gul'dan if he agreed to lead the Horde to Azeroth. Through Medivh, Sargeras told the warlock that he could become a living god if he found the undersea tomb where the Guardian Aegwynn had placed Sargeras' crippled body nearly a thousand years before.

3.title: The Dark Portal and the Fall of Stormwind

texts.text: Gul'dan agreed and decided that once the denizens of Azeroth were beaten, he would find the legendary tomb and claim his reward. Assured that the Horde would serve his purposes, Sargeras ordered the invasion to begin.

4.title: The Dark Portal and the Fall of Stormwind

texts.text: Through a joint effort, Medivh and the warlocks of the Shadow Council opened the dimensional gateway known as the Dark Portal. This portal bridged the distance between Azeroth and Draenor, and it was large enough that armies might pass through it. Gul'dan dispatched orc scouts through the portal to survey the lands which they would conquer. The returning scouts assured the Shadow Council that the world of Azeroth was ripe for the taking.

5.title: The Dark Portal and the Fall of Stormwind

texts.text: Still convinced that Gul'dan's corruption would destroy his people, Durotan spoke out against the warlocks once more. The brave warrior claimed that warlocks were destroying the purity of the orcish spirit and that this reckless invasion would be their doom. Gul'dan, unable to risk killing such a popular hero, was forced to exile Durotan and his Frostwolf Clan into the far reaches of this new world.

6.title: The Dark Portal and the Fall of Stormwind

texts.text: After the exiled Frostwolves charged through the portal, only a few orc clans followed. These orcs quickly set up a base of operations within the Black Morass, a dark and swampy area far to the east of the kingdom of Stormwind. As the orcs began to branch out and explore the new lands, they came into immediate conflict with the human defenders of Stormwind.

7.title: The Dark Portal and the Fall of Stormwind

texts.text: Though these skirmishes usually ended quickly, they did much to illustrate the weaknesses and strengths of both rival species. Llane and Lothar were never able to gather accurate data of the orcs' numbers and could only guess at how great a force they would have to contend with.

8.title: The Dark Portal and the Fall of Stormwind

texts.text: After a few years the majority of the orcish Horde had crossed into Azeroth, and Gul'dan deemed that the time for the primary strike against humanity had come. The Horde launched its full might against the unsuspecting kingdom of Stormwind.

9.title: The Dark Portal and the Fall of Stormwind

texts.text: As the forces of Azeroth and the Horde clashed across the kingdom, internal conflicts began to take their toll on both armies. King Llane, who believed the bestial orcs to be incapable of conquering Azeroth, contemptuously held his position at his capital of Stormwind. However, Sir Lothar became convinced that the battle should be taken directly to the enemy, and he was forced to choose between his convictions and his loyalty to the king.

10.title: The Dark Portal and the Fall of Stormwind

texts.text: Choosing to follow his instincts, Lothar stormed Medivh's tower-fortress of Karazhan with the help of the wizard's young apprentice, Khadgar. Khadgar and Lothar succeeded in vanquishing the possessed Guardian, whom they confirmed to be the source of the conflict.

11.title: The Dark Portal and the Fall of Stormwind

texts.text: By killing Medivh's body, Lothar and the young apprentice inadvertently banished the spirit of Sargeras to the abyss. As a consequence, the pure, virtuous spirit of Medivh was also allowed to live on... and wander the astral plane for many years to come.

12.title: The Dark Portal and the Fall of Stormwind

texts.text: Although Medivh had been defeated, the Horde continued to dominate the defenders of Stormwind. As the Horde's victory drew nearer, Orgrim Doomhammer, one of the greatest orc chieftains, began to see the depraved corruption that had spread throughout the clans since their time in Draenor.

13.title: The Dark Portal and the Fall of Stormwind

texts.text:
His old comrade, Durotan, returned from exile and warned him yet again of Gul'dan's treachery. In speedy retribution, Gul'dan's assassins murdered Durotan and his family, leaving only his infant son alive. Unknown to Doomhammer was the fact that Durotan's infant son was found by the human officer, Aedelas Blackmoore, and taken as a slave. 

That infant orc would one day rise to become the greatest leader his people would ever know.

14.title: The Dark Portal and the Fall of Stormwind

texts.text: Incensed by Durotan's death, Orgrim set out to free the Horde from demonic corruption and ultimately assumed the role of warchief of the Horde by killing Gul'dan's corrupt puppet, Blackhand. Under his decisive leadership the relentless Horde finally laid siege to Stormwind Keep.

15.title: The Dark Portal and the Fall of Stormwind

texts.text: King Llane had severely underestimated the might of the Horde, and he watched helplessly as his kingdom fell to the green-skinned invaders. Ultimately King Llane was assassinated by one of the Shadow Council's finest killers: the half-orc, Garona.

16.title: The Dark Portal and the Fall of Stormwind

texts.text: Lothar and his warriors, returning home from Karazhan, hoped to stem the loss of life and save their once-glorious homeland. Instead, they returned too late and found their beloved kingdom in smoking ruins. The orcish Horde continued to ravage the countryside and claimed the surrounding lands for its own. Forced into hiding, Lothar and his companions swore a grim oath to reclaim their homeland at any cost.

17.title: The Dark Portal and the Fall of Stormwind

texts.text: Mordent Evenshade
<This page is missing.>

I have been unable to summon the courage to recall what I had witnessed these recent days. Even now, I shake at the mere thought, handwriting nigh illegible to my own eye. But I must do so, I must document this, for reasons you will immediately understand.

We had thought the thunder of that late night to be a storm just across the mountainside. It wouldn't be the first time since departing Eldre'Thalas. There was a rumble in the air that never faded, to which I seemed to be the only one bothered. Shortly before sunrise, I followed it through the most forgiving path up the mountain, well beyond where the forests could reach. I expected the highest horizon to give way to an immense valley, but I never could have anticipated what else awaited my view.
<This page is missing.>
<This page is missing.>
<This page is missing.>

A grim idea intruded upon my thoughts. I realized in that moment that we were presented an opportunity. Perhaps we could prolong our immortality by siphoning from these undying creatures and this strange rift. So long as we avert our eyes away from their own, they are seemingly harmless. We could afford ourselves time to create a suitable substitute for the Well of Eternity. At the very least, Eldre'Thalas could be a sanctuary. Presumably a mere few hundred years could be enough time to resolve this newfound hardship. I have faith in our scholars and sorcerers.

After a predictably cacophonous Highborne debate, we decided to return to the city to seek audience with Prince Tortheldrin. We would then share our discovery, and plan for our people's future.

$N, you've got a good sword arm and I've taken notice. 

Things are a fine mess here on Zephras Isle, no doubt about it. We need our fighting shen'dorei in top form if we are to survive what's to come. It's time for you to stop playing at being a proper $c, and actually become one.

Find me inside the base of the watchtower here in Thendal Village. I'll see to it you are properly trained.


-Blademaster Ren, $C Trainer

Greetings, $N,

Since the elemental wind spirits vanished, Zephras has been on a deadly precipice. The birds, the beasts, and even the roots beneath our feet call to us for aid.

Seek me out on the ground floor of the great tree here in Thendal Village. I will counsel and train you in the druidic arts.

-Xyton Silverwind, $C Trainer

Oh yeah. Us gots it right here.

npc:10721.text: Are you here to prove yourself as well?

npc:11026.text: Ah, what a beautiful day to blow something up!
You need to start learning things that are beyond my expertise! Talk to Lilliam Sparkspindle in front of the tent there. He'll set you on the right course!

Trapped inside, they are feverish with the corrupted haze that flows from the evil garden growing there.$B$BPlease, you must help.

npc:13699.text: My sisters and I have come down from the Stonetalon Mountains to put to rest a tragedy from ages past. Unfortunately, we are not powerful enough to accomplish our goals on our own and now seek mortals such as yourself to aid us.$B$BIf you are powerful enough, then we have much to discuss, $c. If you are not, then, for your safety, I will leave the details of my mission out of our conversation.

npc:13717.text: I need no home to know I still have a place in this world, $c. The tribes will see... all of them. They fight amongst one another, and for what? Scraps left over by vultures... lands infested by the Legion... bah!$B$BThe centaur should be proud of their heritage--it is just as noble as any Night elf's or orc's--it is time we started acting like it!

npc:14731.text: Lard keep peace here. Lard also sell fish. Want fish?

npc:14740.text: Fishing is just so pleasant, mon. You know? I owe my state of bliss to my mentor, the greatest angler in the whole world - Nat Pagle. Have you heard of him, mon?$B$BIf you be looking for enlightenment, Nat Pagle be the one who gonna show you the way.

npc:14754.text: Zug zug, my friend!  I am Kelm Hargunth, the main supplier for the Warsong Outriders.  As you improve your standing with the Outriders, I will make available to you a fine selection of goods that you can use inside Warsong Gulch.  Should you find yourself in need of item repair, I also provide those services.

npc:14822.text: I have long known you'd seek me out, $n.$B$BEvery sentient being in this world is driven by the choices they make.  Choices begat further choices, and these in turn make someone who they are.  This is where your fortune is drawn from - who you are, and the choices you make.$B$BAre you ready to discover where your fortune lies?

Very well then...$B$BYou have been tasked by your liege to guard his fields of corn from poachers and thieves.  One night on patrol, you stumble across a haggard man in thread-bare clothing stealing corn from the field.  You quickly confront him, and he immediately begs for his life.  He claims he is stealing the corn to feed his family since the lord of the land - your liege - demands too much in taxes.  Your liege is indeed known for his harsh taxes throughout the land.$B$BMake your choice.

Your fortune is cast, $c.  For the next few hours, you will find your spirit in tune with your true nature.  Be careful, as your fortune - and your fate - are never as clear as you might think them to be.$B$BIf you would like a small glimpse of something to ponder in your future, by all means let me know.  I'd be happy to give you a written fortune, provided you have room in your inventory.  It is one drawn from the insight you have shown in answering my questions.

Your next choice awaits.$B$BYou are the sworn executioner for your liege.  A man has been sent to you for execution as a traitor of the liege and your people.  You know this individual as a close, virtuous friend who mysteriously vanished one day.  You also know that the man's crimes for which he was convicted supposedly caused the deaths of many innocent civilians.  Upon seeing you he begs for his life, claiming he was framed by a higher authority.$B$BMake your choice.

npc:14828.text: Step right up, step right up! If you have tickets from the Darkmoon Faire you'd like redeemed, then just say so! You can redeem tickets in various denominations for wondrous and fantastic prizes. Don't be shy, give it a try!

npc:1496.text: Take it, then. It seems Zygand is too busy for the agonizing trip here to retrieve it himself.

npc:15021.text: We must not allow the Alliance to expand their power base in Arathi!  Even their miniscule Refuge Pointe may one day grow to threaten us.

As you improve your standing with us, I will make available to you a fine selection of goods that you might find useful.  Should you find yourself in need of item repair, I also provide those services.

npc:15350.text: War is upon us, $n.  It's time for every member of the Horde to answer the call and join the fight against the cowardly Alliance.

npc:1569.text: No other race on Azeroth has suffered as much as our people, $c. To laugh in the face of death has become second nature for all of us.

npc:1573.text: The Wildhammer dwarves might have fast steeds, but can those Aerie Peak gryphons stand the heat of The Great Forge?  I think not!

The Wind Spirits have left us.

We've got plenty of drink if you're thirsty, and plenty of bouncers if you're antsy.$B$BNow then... what can this humble servant of the Steamwheedle Cartel do for you?  Better still - what can you do for me, eh?

npc:251361.text: What do you need of me, child of Zephras?

npc:251371.text:
Greetings... Windshaper.

Those that call themselves members of the Windshapers find little common cause with most members of the High Order, as I'm sure you are aware. Outside the relative harmony of Thendal Grove, you may find that these divisions run deep indeed and rivalry can give way to outright violence, in some cases.

I'll say nothing more on this, save that you should mind your own business and do not interfere with the High Order's goals once you leave the grove. This is likely the only warning you'll receive.

Zephras is in great danger. The elemental wind spirits that brought us here to Skywall so many thousands of years ago have abandoned us, leaving us vulnerable in this unstable realm. Our once-robust society spanned multiple island sanctuaries in our corner of Skywall, but now we are not even sure if any other shen'dorei remain outside of this small island.

Things are dire, but the High Order is committed to rising to this challenge.

npc:251373.text: If you have the aptitude for the druidic arts, I can train you.

npc:251376.text:
The hunters and rangers of Zephras have never been more needed. The winds grow ever harsher, and the magic that sustains our island is fading. The wilds have never been more wild, and people like me are needed to keep our people safe.

If you have the proper aptitude as a hunter, I can give you the tools to survive the wilds.

npc:251487.text: What may I do for you, fellow windshaper?

npc:251507.text: Greetings, hunter. I can teach you skills and techniques.

npc:251905.text: If you need training as a cook, I have a few tips and tricks I could pass on! Ho ho! Throw on an apron and let's get started!

npc:251906.text: I'm in charge of Shen'dar Village operations, and there's a lot of things to keep track of around here. Between bandits, cultists, and other random incidents that pop up, keeping this village afloat is a lot of work.

npc:251991.text:
The clothcraft of the Shen'dorei is a harmonious imitation of the flowing, carefree currents of the winds. While the spirits have left us, and I know not when I may see them dance once more... I find great comfort in my art, if only as a distraction.

I can teach you to work the cloth as well, if you'd like to learn?

npc:251993.text: I can teach you to craft fine leather armor, if you have the aptitude.

npc:253471.text:
Welcome to Shen'dralas, or what remains of it.

I hope you can appreciate the majesty of this place, even if it is a haunted shell of its former self.

I suspected that my fallen brethren would be too stubborn to pass on from Eldre'Thalas completely, and assumed they would either haunt those halls for eternity or venture north to this place here to live out whatever afterlives they sought out for themselves. I painstakingly created these crystals to anchor their spirits more closely with Azeroth, allowing them to experience the world almost as though they were alive.

Indeed, it worked then. And I suspect it is working again now. I think they will be appreciative of you restoring some of their corporeality.

You should go meet them.

The full story requires time that I suspect you do not have, so I will attempt to be brief.

Perhaps the simplest way I can put it: these crystals are anchors. They can be used to permanently--well, so long as the crystals hold I suppose--bind something, someone, or even somewhere onto our plane of Azeroth. Prince Tortheldrin ordered the creation of similar pylons when he chose to bind the demon Immol'thar. Some of the Shen'dralar protested this decision and proposed a compelling alternative, but ultimately the prince was uninterested in debate and eager to silence dissent.

I had an opportunity to study their design before it became too unsafe for me to stay within the city's walls and I fled back to Shen'dralas.

The proposed alternative to demonic entanglement was at odds with what Tortheldrin had already set in motion. Given that he was working with power that tends to cloud one's judgment, it's no surprise that his first instinct was to lash out.

Most everyone who pushed back against his plans to summon and bind a demon were slain that day. Some escaped, including some of my own kin that stood in opposition to the prince, but I have yet to meet other survivors of that schism even after all these thousands of years.

npc:254578.text:
The whole of this valley was once a garden of Eldre'Thalas, but that blighted land ahead of us was the highlight of it all. Nearly everyone contributed to its arrangement and growth. When tensions were high, often many of us would take a stroll to clear our minds.

Had it withered purely from neglect, I suspect it would look no different than the rest of Shen'dralas.

npc:254674.text:
I tended to these gardens long ago. I plucked the weeds. Trimmed the shrubbery. Planted the flowers. Alongside an elven woman, and her enchanted amulet.

Time passed. My bark aged. Weeds retaliated. Bushes wilted. Flowers withered. My branches were stiff and my movement slow, yet the elf and her people still smiled. What I could no longer do, they did in my stead.

But they stopped suddenly. This valley grew quiet. Dark. But all was well, with the elven woman's gift. Then, it was taken.

I was left with no choice. I set myself aflame. To burn it all down. So the restless weeds would not spread further.

I have died, but I still burn. The weeds still grow. I have failed.

npc:255486.text:
Ah, it's you! The one who "borrowed" our mana sieve. As much as I would love to give you a very stern talking to for mishandling precious artifacts, the fact that we can communicate at all is a sign you must have done something right with it.

Despite that, I must insist you do not touch it again. Ever.

npc:255829.text: Ogres no longer servants. Strong fists help make new path.

npc:255894.text:
Ah, a worldly explorer!

Can you smell that fresh, ocean air? Just don't inhale too deeply. Sometimes it smells a bit fishy.

npc:255895.text: Hey, hey! What can I do for ya?

npc:255993.text: As experienced as one might be, I urge you to travel with caution. These plains are home to ferocious beasts and others who seek to remove us from these lands. Even the skies have become too dangerous for our wyverns.

npc:256386.text: We've had trouble with shipments going missing across Azeroth. If you find any, I'd appreciate if you could return them to me.

npc:256388.text:
Greetings and well met, $n! Your arrival is timely, and we here at the Durotar Supply and Logistics company are always in need of new contractors.

If you are someone with a knack for gathering useful materials or the skills to craft something from scratch, you have a place here.

Please let me know if you have any questions.

I am glad you asked! We are far more than just a delivery service, $n. We employ and contract craftsmen across a variety of specialties and trades, and keep our ear to the ground for any new opportunities to keep their hands busy and goods flowing. We cannot possibly predict the emergent needs of any potential client, so we depend on their crafting orders to arrive to us.

You can imagine that this pipeline is... not as effective as we would hope. We encourage any crafters to satisfy these demands and deliver the goods directly to the customers, wherever they may be. Worry not, you will be fairly compensated for your troubles and earn respect among our organization.

npc:256390.text: We've had trouble with shipments going missing across Azeroth. If you find any, I'd appreciate if you could return them to me.

npc:256418.text: The blood of our enemy across these plains has only led to the flourishing of these lands.

npc:256655.text: Cooking is a life long pursuit and I see we share the same passion!
Wulan in Shadowprey Village can sell you the "Expert Cookbook".  You will need that if you are to better yourself.
Dirge Quikcleave of Gadgetzan is a master of the culinary arts.  To better yourself you will need to seek him out.

npc:256657.text: Orcs don't kill humans. Weapons do. And I make weapons.

npc:256675.text: You must be tired from your travels. Take rest while you can.

npc:256728.text: Dry winds carry the salt of the sea. Cracked skin and burning eyes are the least of your concerns out here.

npc:257018.text: Ko, i waldir Regenthor. A garde lo thor ve borne nud hamerung ador garde bur agol cynegold.

npc:257554.text: <The gaze of the ranger standing before you is fixed on the enormous anchor pylon in the distance.>

npc:258930.text: You've come for training in order to pass it on to your pets?

npc:259988.text: Me like tiny orcling Nassag. Nuzztok? What his name again? Orcs have funny names.

npc:260383.text: Kor'kron don't leave our own behind. I need you to get some allies and get into that keep. Find the Commander and get him out of there. The fight was all but over as we made our escape, and I'm sure the humans would have taken him prisoner.

Let's just say that the naga were as surprised to see us as we were to see them. We had no choice but to turn and fight. The remaining guards in the keep noticed the commotion and came out in force.

Before we knew it, we were fighting a three-way battle. It was total chaos. We lost half our number in the first minute or two, so the Commander called a retreat.

Taken prisoner, I think. He was covering our rear while I led the retreat, but I saw him take a war hammer to his axe arm and another to his helm. He went down hard. I'm sure he was badly injured, but he was still moving when I lost track of him.

We made it back to the dock but the naga had sunk our skiff. The other two survivors died shortly after, and until you came along, I suspected I'd not be far behind them.

We got caught in a damned battle, that's what happened. We were dispatched here to infiltrate the dungeons beneath the keep on Alcaz Isle and extract a high-value target.

We had just taken out the human guards outside and were about to enter the depths of the keep when we were flanked by a force of naga. Apparently they had their own designs on the place!

npc:260558.text: I can teach you fishing skills.

npc:260559.text: Look at that view, would ya? Don't get much better than this.

npc:260566.text: Ain't nothing ever gonna compare to the smell of freshly discharged gunpowder, friend.

npc:260857.text: Nothin' like a good view of the port so you can call first dibs on shipments.

npc:260931.text: No talk! Must dig! Twilight say Clubtoe dig. Clubtoe dig.

npc:263113.text: It can get boring up here, you know. I can only annoy that stuffy wretch Halaan so much before even that gets old.

npc:268.text: Greetings, $c! I have but one goal: the cataloging and recording of all knowledge related to the history of Duskwood and Darkshire. Perhaps you could help me in my endeavor?

npc:269647.text:
Greetings, $n. You will have to forgive me for not being able to rise and introduce myself properly. I am still recovering from a recent encounter.

I am Mus'hale, an adventurer much like yourself, with a desire to learn of all the various cultures I encounter on my travels.

npc:270582.text:
Greetings, $c.

I can show you how to weave magic about yourself to change the appearance of your equipment, if you so desire. Do you wish to utilize my services?

npc:2834.text: You will need to find Nat Pagle in Dustwallow Marsh to get any better than you are currently.

npc:2851.text: Where would you like to fly to?

npc:2855.text: I know a few things, but I'm no expert. Lucky for you, Magar is. He's standing near the back of the shop. See if he can help you, but be careful not to rile him. He can be irritable.

npc:2857.text: Who says Orcs aren't smart? It takes a lot of brains to be an engineer!
You know who's really smart? Nogg! Smarter than me, even. You go tell Nogg Thund sent you! You can find him by the control panel over there.
You think you're smart enough? You think you got what it takes? Let's find out!

npc:2858.text: How may I be of service?

npc:2861.text: Where would you like to fly to?

npc:2921.text: How perfect of you to come by, $c.$B$BMy name is Lotwil Veriatus, founding member of the Enlightened Assembly of Arcanology, Alchemy, and Engineering Sciences: we seek to blend the intelligent sciences of Azeroth together into one comprehensive school.

npc:2934.text: Knowledge is both tool and weapon to those with the will to use it.

npc:295.text: Welcome to my Inn, weary traveler. What can I do for you?

npc:2980.text: Greetings, $N, and welcome to Camp Narache. News of your arrival spread quickly among the tribe.

npc:2995.text: When mounted on the back of a wind rider, one sees that its reputation for strength and speed is well earned.

npc:3009.text: When I first saw the undead, I wept, for I could not imagine their horror and loneliness. The Earth Mother spoke to me then; she sang in my blood. And she told me, "Save them."

npc:3043.text: No matter how much one learns, there is always more to know.

npc:3052.text: Come closer, young one.  In my time I could hear the flutter of a prey's beating heart, but now you must speak up if you want your words heard.

npc:3061.text: Do you prefer guns or bows?

npc:3065.text: $R have a passion for hunting; it is something that runs deep with our kind.

npc:3084.text: Brek Stonehoof can be found at Stonehoof Geology on the lower rise and can teach you the proper way to harvest precious ores and gems.

npc:3136.text: Don't come out of the shadows like that. Next time give a girl some warning.

npc:3150.text: This here is the finest, most state of the art mode of transportation money can build. What? Deeprun Tram? Gnomes? Listen pal, If you believe that garbage then I've got a statue down in Stranglethorn to sell ya. Now, are you walking to Grom'Gol or are you gonna ride in style in this fine flying machine? Your choice.

npc:3216.text: Listen closely to what you are told and do not quickly trust, or distrust.  For even friends serve their own ends, $c.$B$BOur great Warchief knows this, and to prove that there are warlocks within the Horde who do not wish to destroy it from within or gain control over it, I have volunteered to aid our young leader in anyway I can.

npc:328.text: Greetings mage.  Shall I provide you with further insight into the world of magic?

npc:3309.text: I guarantee this bank's security with my own blood, is that good enough for you?
Besides the Grunts outside, my brothers and I fought at the battle of Hyjal. Any who seek to steal from the bank must face us first.
Would you rather trust your goods with a goblin?

npc:3310.text: You haven't lived until you've looked down on the world from the back of a wind rider.

npc:3318.text: Would you rather trust your goods with a goblin?

npc:3320.text: Would you rather trust your goods with a goblin?
Besides the Grunts outside, my brothers and I fought at the battle of Hyjal. Any who seek to steal from the bank must face us first.
I guarantee this bank's security with my own blood, is that good enough for you?

npc:3344.text: The spirits have guided you to me. How may I be of service?

npc:3345.text: You may have what it takes. Let's find out!

npc:3354.text: Are you here for training?  Or are you just here to waste a warrior's time.

npc:3355.text: Welcome to my forge, Blacksmith. Let me share with you a little secret. No one, no one in the world can you trust. Not men, not women, not beasts ... this you can trust, Steel.

npc:3363.text: About time you showed me some results! Now I'll show you results!

npc:3368.text: I have the finest meats in Orgrimmar.

npc:3412.text: If there were just a few more hours in a day...
Every day is a test, and this day is no different. If you pass this test, I will share some of my knowledge...
You have earned the privilege of training with a higher instructor. Go see my pal Roxxik there.

npc:3413.text: Hello, $n! If you don't see it in my shop, chances are good I can get it!

npc:3539.text:
My blades don't glisten, glitter, or gleam, and they'll sing no epic songs about my creations when I'm gone. 

One thing you can be sure of though is that my weapons will cut down all the knights in Stormwind before losing their honed edge.

npc:3615.text: My wind riders are trained to fly quickly through the hot Barrens air.

npc:3691.text: I know these forests as if they were a part of me... But know that there is still much to be learned from them, and much danger still hidden.

npc:377.text: Do not turn your back on the Light, $c, it may be the one thing that saves you some day.

npc:4453.text: Be careful where you put that foot of yours, mister. We're not all blessed with the lofty height of a $r.
Be careful where you put that foot of yours, mister. We're not all blessed with the lofty height of a skyborne.

npc:4551.text: How may I be of service?

npc:4568.text: Greetings.  I'm an undead mage trainer, and you're a mage.

npc:4576.text: Good! I can tell that my efforts will not be wasted!
I will instruct you when the time is right... that time is not now. You have much more to learn first!

npc:4586.text: The Dark Lady has said that knowledge will be our greatest weapon in this war.

npc:4591.text: Balai Lok'Wein of Brackenwall Village in Dustwallow Marsh sells a manual that you will need to study in order to improve your skills!
I can train you in First Aid techniques.

npc:4616.text: Hmm, you scratch my back, I'll scratch yours. If you do what I ask, and do it well, maybe we can discuss your training.

If I wasn't stuck here day in and day out, I would have attained the mastery required to train the likes of you! Unfortunately that's not the case. Go talk to Hgarth at the Sun Rock Retreat in the Stonetalon Mountains.

npc:4631.text: I see some interesting characters come and go here at the port. Watch yourself, $n. It's never clear who to trust, what with all of the shady activity that goes on here...

npc:514.text: If you'd like to learn how to blacksmith your own weapons and armor, I'd be happy to help.

npc:5512.text: Don't let the humans in the Bazaar fool ye $g lad : lass;, with the subway those gnomes built it's easier than ye might think to transport goods from Ironforge. If they try to tack on import fees just tell them yer gonna buy yer gear from me.

npc:5513.text: I came from Ironforge to help out with the rebuilding effort here. If I can teach enough of ye my skills then maybe I can leave it to ye and take myself back home.

npc:5514.text: Don't let the humans in the Bazaar fool ye $g lad : lass;, with the subway those gnomes built it's easier than ye might think to transport goods from Ironforge. If they try to tack on import fees just tell them yer gonna buy yer gear from me.

npc:5516.text: Look at the wisdom and knowledge of the beast, and you will see yourself. Observe as the owl does, learn cleverness from the sabercat, embody the mighty spirit of the wolf.

npc:5518.text: Quid pro quo! I'll teach you what I know, but first I want you to perform a small task...
Well, you're just zooming right along! I can't teach you anything you don't already know, but Springspindle Fizzlegear sure can! You can find Springspindle in Ironforge. Good luck!

npc:5519.text: If you insert tab A into slot B then of course it's going to go BOOM! Here, let me show you what I have and then you can ask Lilliam about how to put it together so it doesn't blow up.

npc:5595.text: What do ye need directions to?

Yer looking to learn how to use a new weapon are ye?  Well, ye should be talking to Bixi or Buliwyf over at the Timberline Arms weapon shop then lad.  They know their weapons from axes to... uh... zweihanders.

npc:5624.text: Graham Van Talen in Rogues' Quarter on outer ring of Undercity.
Us know her good.  She Mary Edras at inner ring of Rogues' Quarter.
You go to inner ring of The Apothecarium.  Lavinia Crowe is there.

npc:5688.text: Rest your weary bones for a spell.

npc:5694.text: The flow of magic is unpredictable and chaotic, of late. What, I wonder, could be the cause of this?

npc:5759.text: I can train you in First Aid techniques.

npc:5814.text: If we are to make these new lands ours then we must have places to rest our battle weary bodies. Lay your axe by the fire and share the stories of your mighty battles.

npc:5819.text:
If you're looking for plate armor, mail armor or shields, I've got the finest in all of Undercity. Most of these pieces are made and repaired here locally, though some are scavenged.

Feel free to browse.

npc:5883.text: Greetings, $c.  Are you here to learn of the hidden arts?

npc:6026.text: Where would you like to fly to?

npc:6094.text: I can train you in First Aid techniques.

npc:6301.text: Greetings $g lad : lass;, if you're looking for the best deals you'll find outside of Ironforge itself, then you've come to the right place.

npc:6491.text: It is not yet your time. I shall aid your journey back to the realm of the living... for a price.

npc:6546.text: Your errand must mean much, $c, to draw you so deep into the marsh...

npc:6568.text: If tailoring is your thing, Vizzklick will most definitely have your supplies. Take a look around, $n, and let me know if you wish to purchase something!

npc:6726.text: Where would you like to fly to?

npc:6737.text: Your body looks worn and your spirit weary. Rest yourself beneath our roof and allow Elune to guide your dreams.

npc:6740.text: Welcome to my Inn, weary traveler. What can I do for you?

npc:6746.text: As the wind on the plains, you are always welcome here.

npc:6747.text: As the wind on the plains, you are always welcome here.

npc:6790.text: Welcome to my Inn, weary traveler. What can I do for you?

npc:6929.text: If we are to make these new lands ours then we must have places to rest our battle weary bodies. Lay your axe by the fire and share the stories of your mighty battles.

npc:7010.text: These are dangerous times, $r.  An ancient evil is rising, and it cares not if you're Horde or Alliance.

npc:716.text: Master Nesingwary has a big hunt ahead of him.  I find helping him prepare for a day in the jungle is much more relaxing than helping him ready for combat.  Although I do miss some of those glorious moments on the battlefield.

npc:7311.text: Greetings, $c.  Are you here to learn of the hidden arts?

npc:7683.text: Welcome to Blue Moon Odds and Ends, $c.  If you have any questions, please let me know.

npc:7733.text: Ah a visitor! Must be an adventurer, we don't get many tourists down this way. Grab a chair and a drink, make yourself comfortable. Say, you look like you have some meat on your bones. You thinkin about competing in the cage matches?

npc:7737.text: As the wind on the plains, you are always welcome here.

npc:7766.text: You'll have to be patient with me, $n. I've got my Spybot inside working on a very delicate matter. I'll be with ya in a second.$B$BOh, and do me a favor, try not to let Lescovar see you... we're about to ambush him.

npc:7804.text: Sul'thraze... the first time I heard the word uttered I was around your age. It meant nothing to me then, as it means nothing to you now. It was not until a warband of trolls coming from Zul'Farrak laid waste to the land that I understood... and feared.$B$BMany will tell you that the Splitblade of Suffering does not exist. That it's a myth; a rumor started to scare children 'straight.' But believe me, $r, it exists.$B$B<Trenton loses focus as he runs his hand across the jagged scar on his face.>

npc:7824.text: Where would you like to fly to?

npc:7853.text: Hello, $n! I am master engineer, Scooty.

npc:7854.text: Welcome to Camp Mojache, brave $c.  How may I assist you this day?

npc:7869.text: The spirits told me you would come, that you would seek me for some reason, but that even you may not know that reason. So, do you know why you are here?

npc:7875.text: We must ensure the survival of this camp at all costs, $c!  Our enemies must not be given any quarter, for they would surely give us none were we to need it.

npc:8020.text: Where would you like to fly to?

npc:8115.text: Incredible power can be found in the spirits or "muisek" of the creatures that we battle against.$B$BLook inside yourself; learn to harness the power of your own spirit, and you will be more powerful than you ever imagined.

Existing in this area are many creatures considered allies of the night elves. The elves have had access to the power within each of these creatures; it is time that the horde be allowed this same satisfaction. I have devised a way that this power can be captured and used for our benefit.$B$BDo not doubt what I tell you, $n. Help me, and you shall see that I speak truth.

npc:8579.text: Greetings, $c.  Though time and drink have dulled my outer senses, my inner eyes remain strong.

npc:8931.text: Welcome to my Inn, weary traveler. What can I do for you?

npc:8962.text: I think my necklace fell in the lake.  My daddy got it for me, and he's gonna be mad now.

npc:8965.text: Hello there $g mister : ma'am;... do you have a little time that you could help us out?  Please?

npc:9356.text: If we are to make these new lands ours then we must have places to rest our battle weary bodies. Lay your axe by the fire and share the stories of your mighty battles.

npc:9501.text: As the wind on the plains, you are always welcome here.

object:20923.text: This monument is dedicated to all those who have fallen in the protection of Stormwind. Our people have weathered unbelievable hardships to retain their freedoms and to control their own destinies. It is here we remember every sacrifice our citizens have made during the first war that riddled our people.

npc:1500.text:
I hope you're well, all things considered.

Sit for a spell, and hear my tale.  It's a tragedy, of course, but one I hope will end in revenge!

npc:1515.text: The Scarlet Crusade is encroaching on our homeland. The foolish zealots do not realize that the loyal servants of The Dark Lady shall see to their demise.

npc:1518.text: The Dark Lady has put forth the challenge.  It is up to us to meet it.

npc:1719.text: Over here, you worthless...! If you want to do something useful, listen quick!

npc:2055.text: The Royal Apothecary Society shall heed The Dark Lady's call to uncover the New Plague and drive Arthas and his heathen Scourge Army from the world once and for all.

npc:2215.text: In order to serve the Dark Lady and Varimathras we need to advance the front on the Human Infestation.

npc:240.text: Ach, it's hard enough keeping order around here without all these new troubles popping up! I hope you have good news, $N...

npc:241.text: Hey there, friend.  My name's Remy.  I'm from Redridge to the east, and came here looking for business, looking for business.  You got any...got any??

npc:2464.text: Grom'Gol's safety is my highest priority.

npc:2497.text: Eh? Ya have business with Nimboya?

npc:2498.text: What what?!?  We all have profit to make... and we won't do it by standing idle.

npc:2501.text: Oy!  You here for a game of knuckles?

npc:253.text: Aha!  Good day, good day, Master $C!  Come, sit down and have a drink.  You have an enterprising look in your eye, and I think you'll find speaking to me worth your time...

npc:253177.text: Behold, outsider. The forbidden lands of Desolace, where once no centaur dared to travel. Times have changed.

npc:256710.text: There are dark powers growing within the Riverglades, $N. We must learn what we can from them, then snuff them out.

npc:258031.text: Stay a while. Look out to the plains and take in the land. A good hunter must come to know the home of her prey like it is her own.

npc:258570.text: My axes thirst for Twilight blood. We must find an opening and strike with vengeance.

npc:259961.text: Lemme tell ya, kid. It ain't easy bein' a wharfmaster. If you heard all the logistics involved in gettin' something as simple as a crate of apples shipped across the sea, it'd make your head spin.

npc:259962.text: Please, grab any open chair ya like. I'll come take your order in a sec.

npc:261.text: Hello, citizen.  You look like a man with a purpose - do you have business with the Stormwind Army?

npc:262399.text: There's money to be made in these hills. Just you wait and see!

npc:263190.text: What you need from ol' Tan'jani, mm?

npc:264.text: At ease, $C.  If you are just passing though I suggest you stick to the roads and only travel by day. If your business is here in Darkshire, consider lending your abilities to The Night Watch.  Our skill is unquestionable but our numbers are small.

npc:265.text: I have sensed your coming for quite some time, $N.  It was written in the pattern of the stars.

npc:2706.text: Thanks to the Warchief, even here in the ruins of our former prison, some hope remains, and the Horde rises anew.

npc:273.text: Keep the door closed, $C.  Never know when the Dark Riders will be passing through again.

npc:2785.text:
Back away!  Stay back!  I have a pack full of blastpowder and I'm not afraid to use it!  I'll blow us all away!

Oh, never mind.  I thought you were someone else....

npc:2817.text:
You must be hard up to be wandering these Badlands, $c.  Hard up like me.

Or maybe you're here because you're crazy.  Crazy, like me.

npc:2988.text: The Outrunners' duty is to ensure the safety of those who travel across the plains of Mulgore. Those that would threaten the safety of the $r homeland risk punishment at our hands.

npc:2993.text: The land has been good to our people, $c. We must be thankful for our good fortune.

npc:344.text: Who is this $c who goes before the Court of Lakshire in the Kingdom of Stormwind?  State your business within this township, $R.  The orc threat to the Kingdom is far too great to squander time in idle conversation.

npc:3441.text:
To hunt a beast, one must know that beast.  One must learn and respect its ways.

To do otherwise is not to hunt.  To do otherwise is merely to kill.

npc:3446.text:
Yes yes yes!  You're just the skyborne I'm looking for!

Sit!  We have much to discuss!!

npc:382.text: I don't have time to chat, citizen, but if you're willing to give us a hand against the orcs, then I'll find a use for you.

npc:3845.text: We elves have a long history.  Let us hope this history does not return to haunt us.

npc:415.text: Hey buddy, do you think you could give me a hand with something?  I'm really in dire straits here...

npc:4485.text: The days grow long, and still no end to the conflicts of these lands can be seen. It takes no spell caster to know that much. Take up a blade while you can, $c. War can come to our doors at any time, and if I'm not mistaken, you look to be one who revels in it.

npc:4791.text: We may not be in open war with the Alliance, but blood is still shed between us.

npc:5394.text: Don't let the heat bother you.  In the Badlands, heat is the least of your worries.

npc:5591.text: This sty's a little shy of comfy, but it has history, so Stonard must be important to someone. I'd wager that's why we stay here. It sure isn't for the view--it doesn't even look like home.

npc:5878.text: My vision has darkened, but there are many kinds of sight...

npc:633.text: It's dark times that have come, $c... All too soon will we lose everything... When the Light will forsake all but those who truly walk under the Light.

npc:6986.text: My name is Dran Droffers, and this over here is my dummy son Malton.  If you need salvage, or are looking to sell salvage, then we're who you need to be talking to!

npc:715.text: Another fine day in the jungle!  It's going to be quite a hunt, I can feel it.  Once Barnil is done cleaning the guns, I'm taking the hunting party deep into the twisting vines.  Not such a bad way for an old war vet to spend his retirement, eh?

npc:737.text: Well, hello there. You seem like you wouldn't be opposed to making some coin, hm? I can tell from the look in your eyes. I am Mogul Kebok, overseer of operations in Azeroth, and if it is riches you seek, perhaps I can make arrangements.

npc:7407.text: The name's Bilgewhizzle, and I am the chief engineer of the Gadgetzan Water Company.  What can I assist you with?

npc:773.text: $C, eh? I am Krazek, Baron Revilgaz's secretary. I know everything about the goings on in this jungle and beyond. Perhaps you'd be interested in knowing the going price on oil in Ratchet? No? Looking for work, maybe? I can help you there.

npc:7777.text: The Gordunni Ogres encroach upon our lands.  We send as many as are willing to face them in the desecrated ruins of Feralas.

npc:7876.text: Some people wonder what we're doing out here in the desert.  Well... if I told you, then you'd stay and try to make our profits!

npc:823.text: Hello there, $c.  Normally I'd be out on the beat looking after the folk of Stormwind, but a lot of the Stormwind guards are fighting in other lands.  So here I am, deputized and offering bounties when I'd rather be on patrol...

object:138492.text: These shards glint with an unnatural sheen.  It is clear that they hide a deep power within.

meta.attribution: Data from Efficient Games (https://efficient.games), licensed under CC BY 4.0.

accept.text: I've been stuck hiding in this ghost town for weeks, and I haven't eaten anything but grubs and weeds!  I need some decent food, and I'm willing to trade well for it.$B$BBring me a feast and I'll pay you handsomely.$B$BI heard Chef Grual at the Scarlet Raven Tavern in Darkshire makes very good Dusky Crab Cakes...

complete.text: You need some Crab Cakes, do you?  Well I might be able to cook some up for you...

objectives.text: Speak with Chef Grual.

accept.text: Garrick Padfoot - a cutthroat who's plagued our farmers and merchants for weeks - was seen at a shack near the vineyards, which lies east of the Abbey and across the bridge.  Bring me the villain's head, and earn his bounty!$B$BBut be wary, $n.  Garrick has gathered a gang of thugs around him.  He will not be an easy man to reach.

complete.text: Hah - you caught him!  You've done Elwynn a great service, and earned a nice bounty!

objectives.text: Kill Garrick Padfoot and bring his head to Deputy Willem at Northshire Abbey.

progress.text: Did you find Garrick's shack?  Are we finally free of that villain?

accept.text: Your first task is one of cleansing, $n.  A clan of kobolds have infested the woods to the north.  Go there and fight the kobold vermin you find.  Reduce their numbers so that we may one day drive them from Northshire.

complete.text:
Well done, citizen.  Those kobolds are thieves and cowards, but in large numbers they pose a threat to us.  And the humans of Stormwind do not need another threat.

For defeating them, you have my gratitude.

objectives.text: Kill 10 Kobold Vermin, then return to Marshal McBride.

accept.text: Hey, mate! Do a favor for a young man who's been fighting more than his fair share of mindless zombies and spiders?$B$BI got this here letter that needs to go to Brill... to an innkeeper named Renee something-or-other. Don't really matter none what her last name is.$B$BAnyway, it's a nice cozy little place full of victims of the plague trying to make their way in the world. And it be a great spot for you to rest too if the need arises. You should check it out... you do and I'll pay you well.

complete.text:
Oh? A letter? Wonderful news! I've been waiting on word from my dear old mother in Deathknell. Such a saint, she is. I wonder how she's holding up.

What? Too cheery? Not buying it, are you?

Well, get lost then... it's really no business who the letter's from anyway. Go on! Get lost!

Come back when you've got some coin to spend... loafer.

Next thing you know, you'll be coming back to rest after a long days adventure or some stupid thing like that.

objectives.text: Deliver the Nondescript Letter to Innkeeper Renee in Tirisfal Glades.

progress.text:
Yes? Yes? What is it?

The forsaken; they certainly do have huge appetites. Make yourself at home... yes, rest those weary bones. My name's Renee if you need anything at all.

accept.text: $n, my scouts tell me that the kobold infestation is larger than we had thought.  A group of kobold workers has camped near the Echo Ridge Mine to the north.$B$BGo to the mine and remove them.  We know there are at least 10.  Kill them, see if there are more, then report back to me.

complete.text: I don't like hearing of all these kobolds in our mine.  No good can come of this.  Here, take this as payment, and when you're ready, speak to me again.  I would like you to go back to the mines one more time...

objectives.text: Kill 10 Kobold Workers, then report back to Marshal McBride.

complete.text: Thanks, $N!  And come back if you want to trade again.

progress.text:
Farming is thirsty work, and I'm always looking for refreshing spring water.

If you have any, then I'm willing to make a trade.

accept.text: Recently, a new group of thieves has been hanging around Northshire.  They call themselves the Defias Brotherhood, and have been seen across the river to the east.$B$BI don't know what they're up to, but I'm sure it's not good!  Bring me the bandanas they wear, and I'll reward you with a weapon.

complete.text: Back with some bandanas, I see.  The Stormwind Army appreciates your help.

objectives.text: Bring 12 Red Burlap Bandanas to Deputy Willem outside the Northshire Abbey.

progress.text: Have you gathered those bandanas for me yet?

complete.text: Tharil'zun was a vicious, crafty orc.  Well done--I'm sure he didn't go down easy.  Here is your reward, $N.

progress.text: Orc pressure from Blackrock is still tense.  But have you at least rid us of Tharil'zun?

accept.text: Your previous investigations are proof that the Echo Ridge Mine needs purging.  Return to the mine and help clear it of kobolds.$B$BWaste no time, $n.  The longer the kobolds are left unmolested in the mine, the deeper a foothold they gain in Northshire.

complete.text: Once again, you have earned my respect, and the gratitude of the Stormwind Army.  There may yet be kobolds in the mine, but I will marshal others against them.  We have further tasks for you.

objectives.text: Kill 12 Kobold Laborers, then return to Marshal McBride at Northshire Abbey.

accept.text: I hate those nasty timber wolves!  But I sure like eating wolf steaks...  Bring me tough wolf meat and I will exchange it for something you'll find useful.$B$BTough wolf meat is gathered from hunting the timber wolves and young wolves wandering the Northshire countryside.

complete.text:
You've been busy!  I can't wait to cook up that wolf meat...

I have some things here you might want - take your pick!

objectives.text: Bring 8 pieces of Tough Wolf Meat to Eagan Peltskinner outside Northshire Abbey.

progress.text: Hey $N.  I'm getting hungry...did you get that tough wolf meat?

accept.text: If you are concerned that the rumors of murlocs are true, then do this -- travel to the eastern Elwynn bridge and speak with Guard Thomas.  He has been stationed at the bridge for the past week and will know the state of the area.$B$BBring me his report.

complete.text: Yes, murlocs have settled in and around the streams of eastern Elwynn.  We don't know why they are here, but they are aggressive and at least semi-intelligent.

objectives.text: Marshal Dughan wants you to speak with Guard Thomas.

accept.text: A few days ago we sent two Guards, Rolf and Malakai, to investigate along the river, and they have not yet returned.  To complete my report, I must know what happened to those men.$B$BTravel north along the river and find the guards... or their remains.

complete.text: Although much has been stripped from the corpse, strewn nearby is a medallion with the words: "Footman Malakai Stone" etched upon it.

objectives.text: Guard Thomas wants you to travel north up the river and search for the two lost guards, Rolf and Malakai.

accept.text: Tell Marshal Dughan of Malakai and Rolf's deaths, and report to him that the Murlocs in eastern Elwynn cannot be contained by our current troop presence.$B$BI know we don't have many troops to spare, but hopefully Dughan can find someone.

complete.text:
Hmm, this news is troubling.  Already our defenses are stretched thin, and losing Rolf and Malakai to those murlocs put us in an even worse position.

If things don't improve, there will be fighting in Goldshire by the week's end!

objectives.text: Report to Marshal Dughan in Goldshire.

accept.text: $n, there's a new threat in Elwynn Forest!  Murlocs are swimming up the streams of eastern Elwynn, scaring away fish and attacking gentle folk!$B$BI warned Marshal Dughan, but he's more worried about the gnolls and the bandits.  He's not convinced that the murlocs are a danger.$B$BPlease, $n, speak to Dughan and persuade him to send more troops to the east!

complete.text:
Yes, I spoke with Remy.  I respect him as a merchant, though all reports of Murlocs to the east have been sketchy at best.

Your concerns are noted, but unless I receive a military report of a murloc threat, we can't afford to send more troops east.

objectives.text: Remy "Two Times" wants you to speak with Marshal Dughan in Goldshire.

accept.text: Upon further searching the area, you find webbed footprints leading east along the shore of Stone Cairn Lake.  In the distance to the east, you can just barely see a Murloc village.$B$BPerhaps Rolf's fate ended there...

complete.text: You find around the neck of the corpse a metal medallion inscribed with the words "Footman Rolf Hartford."

objectives.text: Search the murloc village for Rolf, or signs of his death.

accept.text: The Kobolds in these parts sometimes carry Gold Dust on them.  I could really use the stuff - bring me a load of it and I'll give you the best price in town...best price in town!$B$BYou can find kobolds in the Fargodeep Mine to the south, and around the Jasperlode Mine to the northeast.

complete.text: Thanks for the dust, $N.  Here's your cash, and...here is a token from associates of mine.  You might find it useful...useful.

objectives.text: Bring 10 Gold Dust to Remy "Two Times" in Goldshire.  Gold Dust is gathered from Kobolds in Elwynn Forest.

progress.text: Psst!  You have that Gold Dust for me...for me?

accept.text: Hail, $n.  Wild animals are growing more and more aggressive the farther we get from Goldshire, and the Eastvale Logging Camp suffers nearly constant attacks from wolves and bears!$B$BWe could use your help out here.

complete.text:
Thanks a lot for the help, $N.  Something in the forest must be making these animals so bold.

Whatever it is, I hope it stays there.

objectives.text: Kill 8 Prowlers and 5 Young Forest Bears, and then return to Guard Thomas at the east Elwynn bridge.

accept.text: $n, you are a $c with proven interest in the security of Northshire.  You are now tasked with the protection of the surrounding Elwynn Forest.$B$BIf you accept this duty, then I have prepared papers that must be delivered to Marshal Dughan in Goldshire.  Goldshire lies along the southern road, past the border gates.

complete.text:
Well, it says here that you've been awarded Acting Deputy Status with the Stormwind Marshals.  Congratulations.

And good luck - keeping Elwynn safe is no picnic... what with most the army busy doing who knows what for who knows which noble!

It's hard to keep track of politics in these dark days...

objectives.text: Take Marshal McBride's Documents to Marshal Dughan in Goldshire.

progress.text:
You have word from McBride?  Northshire is a garden compared to Elwynn Forest, but I wonder what Marshal McBride has to report.

Here, let me have his papers...

accept.text: As Commander of The Night Watch it is my sworn duty to protect the citizens of Darkshire.  Stormwind has retracted their commissioned guards from their posts here, leaving us to our own devices.$b$bIf you feel worthy of the task, we need your help! Assist The Night Watch by venturing forth into Tranquil Gardens, just south of Darkshire, and slaying 8 Skeletal Warriors and 6 Skeletal Mages.  The undead threat must be thwarted!

complete.text: Splendid, $N.  For your service to the people of Darkshire you shall be rewarded.

objectives.text: Commander Althea Ebonlocke of Darkshire wants you to kill 8 Skeletal Warriors and 6 Skeletal Mages.

accept.text: $n, I'm getting reports of an undead infestation in the forest!  If you're up to the job, journey to the Raven Hill graveyard and slay 15 of those vile Skeletal Fiends and 15 Skeletal Horrors.  There are also reports of skeletons just south of Darkshire, in and around Tranquil Gardens Cemetery.  The undead must be driven from Duskwood!

complete.text: The people of Darkshire thank you, $N.  You have proven yourself to be a great ally of The Night Watch.

objectives.text: Commander Althea Ebonlocke of Darkshire wants you to kill 15 Skeletal Fiends and 15 Skeletal Horrors.

accept.text: The situation in Raven Hill is still grim.  The safety of Darkshire is in your hands, $n.  I don't have enough Watchers to keep the town safe.  We need you to dispatch for Raven Hill yet again and rid the eastern mausoleum of 20 Plague Spreaders!

objectives.text: Commander Althea Ebonlocke of Darkshire wants you to kill 20 Plague Spreaders in the eastern Raven Hill mausoleum.

accept.text: For your shrewdness and valor, I have a marker here that is good for one piece of armor.  I want you to take it to Sara Timberlain at the Eastvale Logging Camp.  Give her the marker, and she will fashion the armor for you.  And after you receive it, $n, use it in the defense of Elwynn.$B$BThe Eastvale Logging Camp is beyond Guard Thomas' post to the east.

objectives.text: Give Sara Timberlain the Stormwind Armor Marker.

accept.text: Hello, $ggood sir:my lady;!  Do you have a moment?$B$BMy brother and I run an apothecary in Stormwind, and I'm here to gather large candles for their wax.  Can you help me?$B$BYou can get large candles from kobolds, and I hear rumors that kobolds are infesting the Elwynn mines ... the Fargodeep mine to the south and Jasperlode Mine to the east.  I suggest looking for candles in one of those places.

complete.text: You were busy hunting kobolds, were you?  Thanks for the candles, $N, and here's your reward...

objectives.text: Bring 8 Large Candles to William Pestle in Goldshire.

progress.text: Did you gather those candles yet?

accept.text: My brother Morgan is waiting in Stormwind for my shipment of candles.  I don't have enough time to make the trip myself, but if you'd like to take him the shipment, he'll pay you well.$B$BI've packed up the candles, and you can find Morgan in our shop, Pestle's Apothecary, in the Stormwind Trade District.

complete.text: Here is your payment ... and while you're here, take a look around!  I'm sure we have a potion or other trinket you'd find useful.

objectives.text: Bring William's Shipment to Morgan Pestle in the Stormwind Trade District.

progress.text: Oh, a shipment from my brother?  Splendid!  Fortune truly shines on me today!

accept.text: The mine in Northshire isn't the only one with problems!  I have reports that the Fargodeep Mine in Elwynn has also become a haven for Kobolds.$B$BExplore the mine and confirm these reports, then return to me.  The mine is almost due south of Goldshire, between the Stonefield and Maclure homesteads.

complete.text: This is bad news.  What's next, dragons?!?  We'll have to increase our patrols near that mine.  Thanks for your efforts, $N.  And hold a moment... I might have another task for you.

objectives.text: Explore the Fargodeep Mine, then return to Marshal Dughan in Goldshire.

accept.text: Last night a horrible disturbance rippled through my veins.  I sensed that my granddaughter, Alyssa, was in great danger.  I consulted the cards and Death stared up at me from the table.$b$bAfter taking a long journey through a dark trance I was able to uncover a clue to this terrifying mystery.  A name came to me, the name of Stalvan.$b$bSeek out the Clerk in the Town Hall and see if you can find out more about this character.  I fear for us all.

complete.text: Ah so Madame Eva sent you. . . .

objectives.text: Seek out the Clerk Daltry in the Darkshire Town Hall.

accept.text: Stalvan, eh?  Let me check the town registry.$b$bStalvan. . .Stalvan. . .let's see.  Ah, here we go!  I have a record of a Mr. Stalvan Mistmantle.  The last recorded address is the Moonbrook Schoolhouse.  My, talk about outdated!$b$bDo me a favor will you, friend?  If you happen to go out to Moonbrook, let me know if you get any update on this fellow.  I like to keep the records clean.

complete.text: The old footlocker creaks open. . . .

objectives.text: Travel to the Moonbrook Schoolhouse and bring back any updated information about Stalvan to Clerk Daltry.

accept.text: You find a Dusty Unsent Letter in the old footlocker.

complete.text: Interesting.  So the chap did spend some time in Moonbrook after all.  It is rather odd the letter never got delivered.  Nonetheless, I shall update the registry.

objectives.text: Take the Dusty Unsent Letter to Clerk Daltry.

progress.text: Ah, I remember you.  You're the one who was asking about that Stalvan fellow.  Did you ever find what you were looking for?

accept.text: Oh my!  Must have missed this the first time.  In the registry, right beneath the first address for Stalvan there's another one listed, only partially scratched out.  Looks like he was headed to The Lion's Pride Inn over in Goldshire.  Might want to check there, $n.

complete.text: Stalvan?  Sure sounds familiar.

objectives.text: Go to The Lion's Pride Inn to see if anyone there has heard of the name Stalvan.

accept.text: The name Stalvan rings a bell.  I remember now.$b$bMany years back, on a stormy night, a messenger came in, seeking refuge for the night.  Near the stroke of midnight, the man ran down the stairs screaming, his face pale with fear.  Still wearing his bedclothes, he disappeared into the downpour.$b$bIn his haste he forgot his letters in the chest upstairs.  He never returned for them. One remains from that Stalvan fellow, intended for the Canal District in Stormwind.  Help yourself to it.

complete.text: You've got some nerve bringing this here.

objectives.text: Retrieve Stalvan's Undelivered Letter from the chest and deliver it to the Canal District in Stormwind.

progress.text: What have ya got there?  Let me take a look at that. . .

accept.text: Now that you have both medallions, deliver them to Guard Thomas at the bridge so that he might know the fate of his murdered guards.

complete.text: You have confirmed my fears, $N.  The murlocs are a threat we cannot ignore.

objectives.text: Deliver Rolf and Malakai's Medallions to Guard Thomas at the eastern Elwynn bridge.

progress.text: Hello, $N.  Have you discovered the fates of Rolf and Malakai?

accept.text: My father was the caretaker of the estate long before I was.  He had to mop the blood up after the massacre.  But that's neither here nor there.$b$bThe last funds of the Flintridge trust have dried up.  Now the last of the family possessions are headed for auction.  Blame the tax vultures.  I guess if you're really itching to learn more you're free to look through this junk.  Who knows what you might find.

complete.text: You slowly slide the lid of the crate off. . . .

objectives.text: Search through the packed up possessions for a clue.

accept.text: Inside the crate you find various objects: musty heirlooms, a family portrait, a few hunting trophies and some old books.  Near the bottom, underneath a ceramic vase, you uncover A Torn Journal Page.

complete.text: I can barely make out those letters.  But that writing style reminds me of something I once saw before my vision became so poor.

objectives.text: The Torn Journal page you discovered provides your next clue.

progress.text: What have you got there?  I cannot see.  My eyesight is very bad.  Put it in my hands.

accept.text: There was a bundle of parchments in the chest upstairs when I moved into this place.  I looked at them once when I first arrived but I gave up once the fog hazed over my peepers. $b$bDo an old, nearly-blind man a favor and check the chest upstairs for anything that might help you in your quest to discover more about this Stalvan character.  I'm pretty sure there's a faded journal page that might be of interest to you.  Bring it to me and I'll help in anyway I can.

complete.text: You found it!

objectives.text: Marshal Haggard wants you to check the chest upstairs for the Faded Journal Page.

progress.text: Did you find that page I mentioned, $N?

accept.text: Thanks to you we know the Fargodeep Mine is infested with kobolds.  Now we need a scout to investigate the more distant Jasperlode Mine.$B$BExplore Jasperlode and confirm any kobold presence.  To reach the mine, travel east along the road until you reach the Tower of Azora.  From the tower, head north and you'll find the mine in the foothills.

complete.text:
Kobolds at the Jasperlode Mine, you say?  Curses!  The situation is worsening by the minute!

Thank you for the report, $N.  But I wish that the news you brought was good news.

objectives.text: Explore the Jasperlode Mine, then report back to Marshal Dughan in Goldshire.

accept.text: I know of someone who might be able to assist you.  Back when I was leading the Stormwind Guard, we used to get drinks at the Scarlet Raven Tavern in Darkshire.  The Innkeeper there, Smitts, was quite an expert on the local lore.  Show him this page and see what he has to say about it.

complete.text: By the Light!  You bet I recognize that handwriting.

objectives.text: Take the Faded Journal Page to Tavernkeep Smitts.

progress.text:
Marshal Haggard sent you?  Why didn't you say so? 

Ah, good ol' Haggard.  Poor chap is going to be completely blind before long.  Anyway, let me see what you've got there.

accept.text: I followed the legend of that Stalvan character for years.  When those visiting nobles were slaughtered a few years back I went with Haggard to investigate.  I found these muddy pages but we were never able to link the handwriting to that crazy man in the woods.  Your trail of evidence proves his guilt.  Take this to Commander Ebonlocke immediately and fill her in on what you've discovered!

complete.text: My, you have proved yourself to be quite a detective, $c.

objectives.text: Take the muddy page to Commander Ebonlocke.

progress.text: This better be good, $c.  Let me see what you have and tell me your tale.  But by the Light, be quick about it.  Darkshire's defense is my number one priority.  I have not the time to squander on dead-end leads.

accept.text: I have had my eye on that creep, Stalvan, for quite sometime.  But if this page was written by the same hand it proves his guilt beyond a shadow of a doubt.$b$bIn all his days keeping the Town Registry, Clerk Daltry has become an expert at identifying handwriting.  Show him this page and see if the writing matches that of the registry signature.

complete.text: Why yes!  The writing on this page does in fact match that of the registry signatures.

objectives.text: Show Clerk Daltry the Bloodstained Journal Page.

progress.text: Back again, $N?  What do you have this time?

accept.text: The Defias gang in Northshire wears burlap masks, but the Defias in Elwynn wear linen which I can use to make fine linen goods.$B$BBring me red linen bandanas and I'll use them to fashion something for you.$B$BDefias gang members have camps pocketed throughout Elwynn.

complete.text:
Ah, these are nice bandanas, if a little rough...

Here you are!

objectives.text: Bring 6 Red Linen Bandanas to Sara Timberlain at the Eastvale Logging Camp.

progress.text: I'm running low on linen, $N.  Do you have any for me?

accept.text: Here you go.  And when you give this pie to that Billy, you tell him I hope he chokes on it!

complete.text:
Mm, yum!  This pie is the best!

I think my memory is coming back to me...

objectives.text: Bring the Pork Belly Pie to Billy Maclure at the Maclure Vineyards.

progress.text: Ugh... I'm starving!  Do you have that pie for me, $N?

accept.text: I lost my necklace, and think that guttersnipe Billy Maclure took it!  He's usually scuttling like a rat around the Maclure vineyards east of here. $B$BGet my necklace back for me, and you'll warm an old widow's heart.

complete.text:
You lost a what?  Well I didn't take no necklace, because I ain't no thief!

I might know who did but...<grin>...I'm too hungry to remember.

objectives.text: Speak with Billy Maclure.

accept.text: Maybe if I got a pie, I could tell you who has that necklace.  And you know, I think that old Bernice lady at that other farm makes great Pork Belly Pies... $B$BMaybe if you gave her some chunks of boar meat from the boars that hang around our farms, and told her what it was for, she'd bake up a pie for you.

complete.text: Though this wild boar meat is tough, simmer it enough and it sure does make for some tasty pie!

objectives.text: Bring 4 Chunks of Boar Meat to Auntie Bernice Stonefield at the Stonefield's Farm.

progress.text:
I don't think it's right feeding the boy who stole my necklace in the first place, but if that's what it takes to get back what's mine, then so be it!

Do you have that boar meat?

accept.text: I was playing near the Fargodeep Mine, and I think I dropped, er...I mean I saw, the old lady's necklace.  Don't ask me how it got there...it wasn't me!$B$BWell anyway, I saw this big, gold-toothed kobold pick up the necklace and run into the mine.  Go find that kobold and you'll find the necklace, I swear!

complete.text:
Oh, you found it!  Thank you, thank you dear!

Here, take this.  It was my husband's and he always said it was lucky.  If only he didn't forget it on his last campaign! *sniff*

objectives.text: Bring Bernice's Necklace to "Auntie" Bernice Stonefield at the Stonefield Farm.

progress.text: Hello, $N.  Have you found my necklace?

accept.text: The Brackwells have a prize-winning pig, Princess.  The sow is HUGE, and she got that way from sneaking over here and eating my veggies!$B$BSo before she comes to our fields...Princess must die!  Bring me her collar as proof of the deed and I'll give you something for your time!$B$BPrincess is usually over at the Brackwell Pumpkin Patch, to the east and beyond the Maclure farm.  Get her before she gets hungry and comes back here!

objectives.text: Kill Princess, grab her collar, then bring it back to Ma Stonefield at the Stonefield Farm.

accept.text: During the last orc invasion we were forced to smelt our iron down to make bullets, swords and armor.
